newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn ruling parties near deal on Eurofighter - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bonn ruling parties near deal on Eurofighter - paper.

text.p: Germany's coalition parties have hammered out in principle an agreement which secures financing for the four-nation Eurofighter project to go ahead this year, the weekly Welt am Sonntag reported.

Under the deal, an extra two billion marks ($1.3 billion) will be found for development of the fighter aircraft between 1998 and 2001, with half coming out of the existing defence budget and half from a special finance ministry allocation, the paper said in an advance release from Sunday's edition.
A final decision on the project would be made by the end of March, it said.
A Defence Ministry spokesman said he was not aware of any financing agreement, but that Defence Minister Volker Ruehe was confident agreement would be reached before the end of March.
Until now, the defence ministry had allocated just 2.8 billion marks in the four-year plan while Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA) had been saying it needed 4.8 billion marks.
Germany wants to buy 180 of the aircraft, to be delivered between 2002 and 2012 or 2015, at a total cost of around 26 billion marks.
Financing problems have been delaying signing of a memorandum of understanding with Britain, Spain, and Italy.
British Aerospace, Alenia of Italy and Casa of Spain are all partners in the consortium together with DASA.
Britain wants to order 232 aircraft, Italy is scheduled to take 140 and Spain 87.

The fact that half the German allocation is to come out of the existing defence budget is likely to mean that Germany, which is committed to around two dozen joint military procurement projects with France, may have to put back some other spending. ($1=1.5492 Mark)
